name: stocklib-6
description: Six fixed, named tasks against a synthetic stdlib-only Python package. Two pairs edit the same region (T2/T5 in ledger.py, T4/T6 at the end of report.py), so a wave that builds both from one base meets a merge conflict that a serial wave cannot. Each task's oracle is a unittest module the coordinator runs at the worker's head in a clean checkout; workers never receive it. `reference` is the edit the inert stand-in applies and the proof that each oracle discriminates (check-prereg): it fails on the seed and passes on the reference, and every order of the six references composes.

# stocklib

A tiny stock-keeping library: the fixed target of open-fleet's pre-registered WIP-curve
experiment (#604). It is synthetic, small and stdlib-only on purpose.

Run the tests with `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t .`

tasks.title: Ledger.remove refuses to overdraw
tasks.statement: Make stocklib.ledger.Ledger.remove raise ValueError when asked to remove more than the quantity in stock for that SKU (an unknown SKU has 0 in stock). A refused removal must leave the stock unchanged. Removing exactly the quantity in stock is allowed and leaves 0.
tasks.oracle:
import unittest

from stocklib.ledger import Ledger


class Oracle(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_overdraw_is_refused_and_stock_unchanged(self):
        ledger = Ledger()
        ledger.add("bolt", 5)
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
            ledger.remove("bolt", 6)
        self.assertEqual(ledger.quantity("bolt"), 5)

    def test_unknown_sku_cannot_be_removed(self):
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
            Ledger().remove("nut", 1)

    def test_exact_removal_empties_the_sku(self):
        ledger = Ledger()
        ledger.add("bolt", 2)
        ledger.remove("bolt", 2)
        self.assertEqual(ledger.quantity("bolt"), 0)

tasks.title: report.to_csv exports the ledger
tasks.statement: Add stocklib.report.to_csv(ledger) returning CSV text: a header row 'sku,quantity', then one row per SKU in sorted SKU order, each line ending in '\n' (including the last). Quote fields per RFC 4180 (use the csv module), so a SKU containing a comma is quoted. An empty ledger yields only the header line.
tasks.oracle:
import unittest

from stocklib.ledger import Ledger
from stocklib.report import to_csv


class Oracle(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_header_sorted_rows_and_quoting(self):
        ledger = Ledger()
        ledger.add("b", 2)
        ledger.add("a,1", 3)
        self.assertEqual(to_csv(ledger), 'sku,quantity\n"a,1",3\nb,2\n')

    def test_an_empty_ledger_is_the_header(self):
        self.assertEqual(to_csv(Ledger()), "sku,quantity\n")

tasks.title: Ledger keeps an audit history
tasks.statement: Give stocklib.ledger.Ledger an audit trail: Ledger.history() returns a list of (operation, sku, qty) tuples, operation 'add' or 'remove', in call order, recording only operations that succeeded (a call that raises is not recorded). history() returns a copy, so mutating the returned list does not change the ledger.
tasks.oracle:
import unittest

from stocklib.ledger import Ledger


class Oracle(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_successful_operations_are_recorded_in_order(self):
        ledger = Ledger()
        ledger.add("bolt", 3)
        ledger.remove("bolt", 1)
        ledger.add("nut", 2)
        self.assertEqual(ledger.history(),
                         [("add", "bolt", 3), ("remove", "bolt", 1), ("add", "nut", 2)])

    def test_a_refused_operation_is_not_recorded(self):
        ledger = Ledger()
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
            ledger.add("bolt", 0)
        self.assertEqual(ledger.history(), [])

    def test_history_is_a_copy(self):
        ledger = Ledger()
        ledger.add("bolt", 1)
        ledger.history().append(("add", "x", 1))
        self.assertEqual(len(ledger.history()), 1)

tasks.title: summary ends with a TOTAL line
tasks.statement: Add stocklib.report.totals(ledger) returning the sum of all quantities as an int, and make stocklib.report.summary(ledger) end with a final line 'TOTAL <n>' where n is that sum. The summary of an empty ledger is exactly 'TOTAL 0'. Every other summary line is unchanged.
tasks.oracle:
import unittest

from stocklib.ledger import Ledger
from stocklib.report import summary, totals


class Oracle(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_totals_and_the_total_line(self):
        ledger = Ledger()
        ledger.add("nut", 2)
        ledger.add("bolt", 3)
        self.assertEqual(totals(ledger), 5)
        self.assertEqual(summary(ledger), "bolt: 3\nnut: 2\nTOTAL 5")

    def test_an_empty_ledger(self):
        self.assertEqual(totals(Ledger()), 0)
        self.assertEqual(summary(Ledger()), "TOTAL 0")
